title: Going Further: How Plants Make Food
subject: science
instructions: Read the passage, then answer each question in its box. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.title: Plants Make Their Own Food
questions.text:
Plants make their own food. This is called photosynthesis. A plant takes in carbon dioxide, a gas in the air, through tiny holes in its leaves called stomata. Its roots take in water from the soil.

Inside the leaves are chloroplasts. They hold a green pigment called chlorophyll, which catches energy from light. The plant uses that energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into a sugar called glucose. That sugar is the plant's food. Oxygen is left over, and the plant lets it out into the air.

Long ago, before tiny living things began making food this way, Earth's air had almost no oxygen. Over a very long time, photosynthesis filled the air with the oxygen that people and animals breathe today.

options.why: Yes: light energy turns them into glucose.

questions.prompt: Big Idea: Why do people and animals depend on plants? Use a detail from the passage.
questions.key: Plants give off the oxygen people and animals breathe (lines 6-7), and/or plants make the food (sugar) that feeds other living things. Full credit needs a reason tied to the passage, such as oxygen in the air; 'they are nice' or no reason is not credit.
